source.title: Assign and Add: A Mechanistic Study of Compositional Arithmetic
source.authors: Brady Exoo; Alberto Bietti; J. Sous

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether progress measures and mechanistic analysis of a small transformer’s algorithmic generalization reveal a developing generalizing circuit. It uses a compositional arithmetic task and measures different from a direct test of the original grokking claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own training dynamics, circuit measurements, and generalization outcomes, which bear on V2. It does not test the overfitting-to-generalization pattern or the effect of training-set size on optimization delay in V1. Results cited from prior grokking work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a study of compositional generalization (variable binding plus modular addition), not of grokking. Training sequences are sampled fresh during training, so there is no fixed small training set and no memorization phase. The paper reports no overfitting followed by delayed generalization and no test of the delay against training-set size. It also never shows memorizing components being removed. The accuracy spikes (steps ~5300–5400 and ~14500–16000) are staged acquisition and late routing correction of a sub-skill: train and test sets rise together at the first spike. The second spike covers only held-out variable positions and is explained by routing of variable b, not by circuit cleanup after memorization. Grokking and the Fourier circuit are cited as background. Matching one neuron to Gromov's Fourier construction in a single run is not a test of V2 or V6. These findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that out-of-distribution generalization arises by composing an independently learned modular-addition Fourier circuit (layer-2 MLP) with a modified induction-head variable-assignment circuit. Training proceeds in three phases: addition first, then variable assignment, then refinement on hard held-out sequences. A theoretical gradient analysis shows how the composing QK2 associative memory arises.
record.recipe_differences: Uses modular addition in a compositional variable-assignment task, rather than testing the original grokking setup or reproducing its overfitting-to-generalization measurement. The paper uses AdamW with weight decay and reports circuit and routing progress measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The timing of the accuracy spikes differs in the alternate initialization; the paper says the alternate run shows the same spikes at different times. In that run, the lowered variable accuracy appears for k on the left-hand side rather than b.

fits_no_version.finding: With freshly sampled data, a 2-layer transformer learns modular addition first, then variable binding (abrupt spike ~step 5300–5400). Last comes a late routing correction (~14500–16000) that lifts out-of-distribution var-restricted accuracy. A variable-binding probe reaches 80% before the first spike.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In compositional arithmetic tasks, sub-skills are acquired in stages with abrupt accuracy transitions that internal progress measures partly anticipate, without a memorization phase.

fits_no_version.finding: The final model's layer-2 MLP implements the known Fourier modular-addition circuit (99.94% isolated-circuit accuracy; neuron 70 matches the k=11 construction) and reuses it for variable and constant operands.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fourier modular-addition circuits are reused as modules when addition is composed with other mechanisms.

fits_no_version.finding: Generalization to unseen addition pairs needs training fraction f ≳ 0.25; generalization to 2-variable sequences needs relative frequency r ≳ 0.2 (both measured at 30000 steps).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compositional generalization in this task has data-coverage thresholds.

record.code_released: not stated (the text says code is available at MechCompose but gives no URL)
record.problems: The mechanistic analysis focuses on a single training run; the alternate run is reported as an accuracy plot. The task and model are deliberately limited in complexity. The paper does not quantify uncertainty for the reported outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: No additional distinct claim-relevant results omitted.

untested.parts: All of it: no fixed small dataset, no chance-level test accuracy after train saturation, no delay-versus-training-set-size measurement (Figure 3 reports final accuracy at 30000 steps only).
All of it: no memorization phase or memorizing-component removal, and no delayed grokking jump for progress measures to anticipate.
All of it: a single weight-decay value, no critical dataset size, no ungrokking test.
All of it: mechanism analysed in one run; the alternate run is shown only as an accuracy plot.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2/tests/V2-supports call is not sustained. The study never sets up grokking (no fixed dataset, no memorization, no train-test gap before the first spike), and its progress measures track staged compositional learning. The only grokking-like result, the delayed var-restricted spike, is an out-of-distribution routing fix for one variable (b in one run, k in the other). The mechanism analysis covers a single run, and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report test accuracy staying at chance after training accuracy saturates, nor whether optimization delay grows as training-set size shrinks.
Does not test whether memorizing components are removed later. Its progress measures and circuit analysis concern modular addition and variable-assignment routing in a compositional task.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale or weight-norm sweep, or lazy-to-rich transition test.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
Uses weight decay in training but does not test whether low norm favours an efficient circuit, or test a critical dataset size or ungrokking.
Does not compare identifiable learned algorithms across runs; it focuses mechanistic analysis on one run.
Does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point softmax limits as causes of delayed generalization.

rows.subject: 2-layer transformer, single training run
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated the isolated subnetwork WU(MLP2(OV2(a) + OV2(b))) on all constant pairs.
rows.measure: Accuracy of the isolated modular-addition subnetwork
rows.note: The authors say this nearly recovers the full model’s performance on the modular-addition dataset.
rows.check: End-of-training accuracy of the isolated OV2-MLP2 circuit (99.94%). This is a final-model circuit check, not a progress measure anticipating a delayed jump after memorization, so it does not bear on V2.

source_check.correct: All 59² constant pairs; the extracted text flattens the exponent to 592. Isolated-circuit accuracy: 99.94%. State: cannot_determine for the grokking claim versions.
source_check.problem: Pair count contains a flattened exponent; final circuit accuracy does not establish a grokking effect.

rows.measure: Match between empirical preactivations and theoretical Fourier feature
rows.note: The paper describes the Fourier-feature mechanism as present in the trained model.
rows.check: One neuron's (70) match to a theoretical Fourier feature, shown qualitatively in a single run. It shows the end-state mechanism, not gradual formation before a grokking jump. It is also not a cross-run comparison bearing on V6.

rows.subject: 2-layer transformer, single training run
rows.operation_detail: Tracked the isolated OV2–MLP2 modular-addition progress measure during training.

rows.note: This tracks early acquisition of modular addition, before the later variable-assignment learning described in the paper.
rows.check: The addition progress measure rises together with 0-var accuracy in the first phase. No delay after training saturation and no memorization phase are reported, so it cannot show progress measures anticipating a grokking jump.

rows.subject: 2-layer transformer, single training run

rows.value: increases; accuracy on var-restricted test sets is brought in line with the rest
rows.note: The paper attributes the improvement to correction of routing, including cases with b as the second operand.
rows.check: Late spike on var-restricted (out-of-distribution variable-position) sets, attributed to routing of b. It is grokking-like only loosely: there is no memorization phase, and data are sampled fresh each step. Train-set saturation timing is shown only in a figure, with no number given.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine. Variable-restricted accuracy catches up between steps 14500 and 16000 as routing improves.

relation.reason: Grokking appears as cited background. The experiments use freshly sampled sequences and do not establish an initial memorization phase followed by delayed generalization.

tranche.reason: The study measures compositional arithmetic and staged circuit acquisition. It does not test the specified grokking versions or use delayed generalization as a tool.

source_check.notes: All rows link to none; their measures cannot determine the grokking versions, so their states should be cannot_determine. Appendix B inconsistently names probe and routing layers; Section 3 and Section 6 also disagree about which operand position excludes b.

reader_labels.reason: Progress measures track modular addition before variable routing; variable-binding measures develop in later phases, alongside the reported accuracy transitions and final generalization (r1–r11).
